q: A Lead Executive Officer is aligning the Health Extension Program (HEP) strategic plan with the Health Sector Transformation Plan (HSTP II). Which strategic approach best ensures long-term operational sustainability of high-value health center assets and community post infrastructure?
options: Developing integrated frameworks that explicitly align institutional goals with local service delivery metrics.
Issuing periodic operational directives instructing Health Extension Workers to increase facility utilization.
Procuring updated diagnostic equipment whenever existing health post infrastructure shows operational wear.
Rebranding health posts to reflect modern community care terminology to enhance public perception.

q: When translating national Primary Health Care policies/strategies into agrarian Woreda operational plans, which approach best addresses equity gaps in remote kebele health service coverage?
options: Enforcing uniform health post opening hours across all kebeles regardless of pastoral or agrarian movement.
Increasing the frequency of standard reporting templates sent from health posts to the Woreda health office.
Reallocating all preventive health budgets toward tertiary hospital referrals for critically ill rural patients.
Adapting service packages through contextualized micro-planning based on local epidemiological profiles.

q: During budget planning, an officer notices that short-term projects provide quick results but may not support long-term government priorities. How should the officer apply strategic thinking?
options: Allocate resources to short-term projects to achieve immediate outputs
Focus only on long-term projects and disregard urgent short-term requirements
Follow previous budgets strictly without reviewing evolving priorities and needs
Balance short-term needs with long-term goals and prioritize initiatives with sustainable impact

q: An office relies on a slow, paper-based process to handle routine client requests, resulting in long delays. A junior staff member proposes a simple digital tracking system using existing office computers, but some colleagues resist because "this is not how things have always been done." Which response best reflects strong innovation competency?
options: Abandon the idea to avoid conflict with colleagues
Pilot the new system on a small scale and refine it
Implement the system for everyone immediately without testing
Report resistant colleagues to management

q: A government agency responsible for supporting small enterprises notices that local producers in a particular sector lack access to information about how to meet quality standards required to enter a larger market. What action best demonstrates this competency?
options: Leave the matter to the private sector to resolve on its own
Identify the specific gaps producers face and provide targeted guidance
Set requirements for producers without consulting them
Wait until producers formally request help before taking any action

q: A government officer is planning a program to improve local business participation in public procurement. Multiple stakeholders including small businesses, community groups and regulatory agencies have conflicting priorities. Which action best demonstrates stakeholder leadership?
options: Map stakeholders, foster dialogue, and build consensus.
Prioritize only the needs of large businesses to ensure project efficiency
Implement decisions without consulting stakeholders to avoid delays
Focus exclusively on regulatory compliance without engaging communities

q: Which statement best reflects the combined essence of communication and influencing?
options: Communicating clearly and ethically to guide decisions toward shared outcomes
Delivering persuasive messages while giving limited attention to stakeholder views
Sharing accurate information through established organizational channels
Persuading others primarily by highlighting personal expertise and authority

q: Which behavior most accurately reflects effective teamwork within a public service organization?
options: Sharing relevant information and resources to achieve shared objectives
Emphasizing individual achievements over collective team results
Restricting collaboration to staff within the same organizational unit
Avoiding disagreement by disregarding differing opinions within the team

q: A civil servant responsible for issuing permits encounters an angry citizen who claims their application was unfairly delayed and accuses the office of bias. Which response best demonstrates emotional intelligence?
options: Remain calm, acknowledge concerns, and explain procedures objectively
Restate the rules firmly and end the interaction quickly
Transfer the interaction to a colleague to avoid involvement
Ignore emotional cues and complete the transaction efficiently

q: A procurement officer is overseeing a tender evaluation. A close acquaintance who owns one of the bidding companies asks informally for information about competitors' bids. Which action best demonstrates ethics and role modeling?
options: Refuse the request, disclose the relationship, and follow proper procedures
Provide limited information without revealing competitor details to assist the acquaintance
Delay responding to the acquaintance until the evaluation process is complete
Share some non-confidential information to maintain the personal relationship

q: A committee is selecting participants for a professional-development program. Most applicants have similar qualifications, but candidates from remote areas and candidates with disabilities have had fewer opportunities to access training. Which approach is most consistent with fair and inclusive public administration?
options: Select according to previous training and current performance because identical criteria guarantee fairness.
Reserve a fixed number of places for underrepresented groups regardless of their qualifications.
Apply job-relevant criteria while considering unequal access to prior opportunities and providing reasonable accommodation.
Select the applicants who are most likely to complete the training quickly and produce immediate institutional benefits.

q: A public service project team includes members from different cultural and professional backgrounds. During meetings, some members rarely speak up, and their perspectives are often overlooked. As the team leader, which action best demonstrates diversity and inclusion?
options: Encourage all members to share ideas and acknowledge perspectives
Focus discussions on the most vocal members to save time consistently
Assign tasks primarily based on seniority to minimize potential conflict
Limit participation only to members with direct technical expertise

q: Your unit has met its annual targets, but staff motivation is declining because employees believe that their work is repetitive and has little connection to public outcomes. As the supervisor, what should you do first?
options: Introduce financial or non-financial rewards for employees who exceed their targets.
Explain how each role contributes to institutional priorities and involve staff
Increase monitoring and reporting requirements to ensure that employees remain focused on their responsibilities.
Rotate staff among different tasks so that everyone experiences greater variety.

q: A citizen approaches your office with a complaint that falls partly outside your unit's formal mandate. The issue is urgent, but assisting the citizen will require coordination with another institution. What best demonstrates public-service servanthood?
options: Explain that the issue is outside your mandate and provide the other institution's contact details.
Clarify the citizen's need, explain the limits of your authority, and facilitate a referral
Resolve the issue yourself, even if doing so requires bypassing established procedures.
Ask the citizen to submit a formal written complaint before providing any assistance.

q: A manager schedules eight consecutive meetings from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. without breaks. After each meeting, the manager must send decisions and assign follow-up actions. What adjustment is most useful?
options: Combine all meetings into one longer meeting
Leave time between meetings for follow-up work
Ask participants to shorten their contributions
Schedule follow-up activities for the following week

q: In a resource-constrained public agency, you are tasked with improving service delivery. Which approach best demonstrates value-adding work?
options: Prioritizing activities that align with citizen needs
Focusing on completing all assigned tasks within the stipulated time
Adopting innovative tools to modernize service delivery processes
Delegating responsibilities to junior staff to enhance their experience

q: A specialized medical equipment deployment project managed by your desk misses its implementation deadline by six months due to poor contractor performance and weak tracking. How do you exercise professional accountability?
options: Initiate legal contract termination procedures against the defaulting vendor.
Present a complete failure analysis and revised milestone recovery plan to leadership.
Reallocate remaining project budgets to high-performing regional sites.
Request an independent audit to establish contractual liability.

q: You are leading a shift toward decentralized hospital budget autonomy. Regional health directors resist, fearing full financial liability and administrative overburden. How do you lead this strategic transition?
options: Mandate immediate compliance as required by national civil service reform laws.
Implement phased autonomy paired with technical financial management coaching
Pause the decentralization process until regional directors request transition.
Maintain central financial approval while delegating routine operational purchasing.

q: Your public health center's maternal waiting home needs basic bedding and nutrition supplies, but the quarterly government budget is already fully allocated. Which approach best reflects responsible resource mobilization?
options: Collaborate with the facility management committee to map local community organizations, NGOs, and municipal partners through transparent, documented in-kind support requests.
Ask patients' families to pay an informal cash fee at the gate to cover supply costs.
Close the maternal waiting home until the next fiscal year budget arrives.
Divert emergency obstetric medications to trade for food supplies.
rationale: Ethical resource mobilization leverages community and institutional partnerships transparently without imposing unauthorized fees on citizens.

q: Your hospital transitions from paper registers to an Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system, and several colleagues complain that the new workflow slows them down. What demonstrates a strong growth mindset?
options: Attend the hands-on training sessions, practice entering records accurately, and help peers troubleshoot common data-entry steps.
Continue using only paper notebooks and leave the digital entry to the data clerk at the end of the month.
Criticize the IT team publicly during morning rounds for introducing a difficult system.
Avoid logging into the EMR unless a supervisor is watching.
rationale: A growth mindset embraces digital health reforms as an opportunity to build new skills and support team adaptation.

q: During a crowded night shift, an anxious parent loudly accuses your clinical team of ignoring their sick child while you are stabilizing another critical emergency. How should you respond first?
options: Keep your voice calm, acknowledge the parent's fear empathetically, briefly explain the triage priority, and give a clear update on when their child will be seen.
Raise your voice to remind the parent that hospital rules prohibit shouting at staff.
Walk away without speaking so you do not get drawn into an argument.
Tell the parent to take their child to a private clinic if they cannot wait.
rationale: Emotional intelligence combines self-regulation under stress with empathetic communication that de-escalates citizen anxiety.

q: At the start of your morning shift, you have four pending tasks: (1) an acutely deteriorating patient needing immediate assessment, (2) a monthly DHIS2 report due at 4:00 PM, (3) routine supply restocking, and (4) organizing staff leave schedules. How should you sequence your work?
options: Stabilize the acute patient first, delegate or schedule routine restocking mid-morning, complete the DHIS2 report well before the 4:00 PM deadline, and finalize leave schedules last.
Finish the leave schedules and DHIS2 report first so paperwork is out of the way before seeing patients.
Handle tasks in whichever order people ask for them throughout the day.
Wait until 3:45 PM to start compiling the monthly DHIS2 report.
rationale: Effective civil service time management prioritizes life-safety clinical urgency first, followed by hard institutional reporting deadlines.

q: As a clinical unit team leader, you notice that infection-prevention compliance has dropped during weekend shifts due to unclear task assignments. What is the most effective leadership action?
options: Hold a constructive review with the weekend team, clarify roles using a visible checklist, ensure supplies are stocked before Friday afternoon, and model compliance yourself.
Issue formal warning letters to all weekend staff without discussing the root causes.
Ignore the weekend gap as long as weekday inspection scores remain high.
Perform all infection-prevention tasks yourself during weekends.
rationale: Transformational public-sector leadership removes operational bottlenecks, clarifies accountability, and leads by example.

q: A newly graduated clinician assigned to your unit hesitates to perform routine procedures independently despite having passed licensure exams. How can you best empower them?
options: Pair them with an experienced mentor for structured observation, provide constructive feedback after each case, and gradually increase their independent responsibilities.
Take over all their clinical tasks so patients are not delayed.
Assign them complex emergency cases immediately without supervision so they learn under pressure.
Reassign them permanently to clerical filing duties.
rationale: Empowerment builds long-term institutional capacity through structured coaching, safe delegation, and confidence-building feedback.

q: Under Federal Civil Servants Proclamation No. 1353/2025, a supervisor instructs you verbally to backdate a training attendance sheet so an absent colleague can receive a per-diem allowance. What is your legal and ethical obligation?
options: Politely refuse to falsify the official record, explain that attendance logs must reflect actual presence, and report the matter through proper ethical channels if pressured.
Sign the backdated sheet because civil servants must always obey verbal orders from a supervisor.
Sign the sheet but add a small pencil mark next to the absent colleague's name.
Ask a junior clerk to sign the form on your behalf.
rationale: Proclamation No. 1353/2025 requires civil servants to uphold legality and integrity; an unlawful instruction to falsify public financial records must not be executed.

q: A medical supply vendor offers you a personal smartphone as a 'thank-you gift' after your department submits a positive technical evaluation of their equipment. What must you do?
options: Decline the gift immediately, document the interaction, and notify your facility's ethics and anti-corruption officer.
Accept the phone quietly as long as it does not change your future evaluations.
Accept the phone and share it with other members of the evaluation committee.
Ask the vendor to donate the phone directly to your personal home address instead.
rationale: Accepting gifts from suppliers creates a direct conflict of interest and violates civil service anti-corruption regulations.

q: When auditing your facility's monthly HMIS report, you find that Accuracy is 98%, Completeness is 96%, Validity is 95%, but Timeliness is only 60% because reports are submitted two weeks late. What is the Data Quality Index (DQI) and operational implication?
options: The DQI is 87.25%, falling below the 95% target; delayed submission prevents woreda and regional teams from responding promptly to disease trends.
The DQI is 96.3%, which meets the 95% target because accuracy and completeness are high.
Timeliness does not affect data quality as long as the numbers are eventually entered.
The facility should estimate missing numbers early to hit 100% timeliness.
rationale: DQI averages all four dimensions ((98 + 96 + 95 + 60) / 4 = 87.25%); late data undermines timely public health decision-making.

q: You share a desktop workstation at the nursing station to access patient EMR records and DHIS2. Which practice best protects patient confidentiality and system security?
options: Use your own unique login credentials and lock or log out of the workstation every time you step away.
Keep one shared password taped under the keyboard so any nurse on shift can log in quickly.
Stay logged into your account all day so the next shift does not have to waste time signing in.
Send patient lab results via public social media groups when the hospital Wi-Fi is slow.
rationale: Individual authentication and automatic/manual screen locking prevent unauthorized access and maintain audit trails for sensitive health data.

q: A woreda health center targets 400 antenatal care (ANC-4) visits per quarter. In Q1, it achieved 340 visits, and in Q2, it achieved 380 visits. By what percentage did performance improve from Q1 to Q2, and what was the Q2 target achievement rate?
options: 11.8% improvement from Q1 to Q2; 95.0% target achievement in Q2.
10.0% improvement from Q1 to Q2; 90.0% target achievement in Q2.
40.0% improvement from Q1 to Q2; 85.0% target achievement in Q2.
11.8% improvement from Q1 to Q2; 85.0% target achievement in Q2.

q: A hospital ward has 24 nurses working across three 8-hour shifts (Morning, Afternoon, Night) in a 3:2:1 staffing ratio. How many nurses are assigned to the Morning shift?
options: 12 nurses
8 nurses
4 nurses
16 nurses
rationale: Total ratio parts = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Each part = 24 / 6 = 4 nurses. Morning shift = 3 × 4 = 12 nurses.

q: Premise 1: All public health facilities must submit monthly DHIS2 reports by the 5th day of the following month. Premise 2: Clinic B submitted its Tikimt report on the 8th day. Which conclusion logically follows?
options: Clinic B did not meet the mandatory monthly DHIS2 reporting deadline.
Clinic B's data is inaccurate and must be deleted.
All clinics in the woreda submitted their reports late.
Clinic B is exempt from DHIS2 reporting.
rationale: Deductive logic confirms only that submitting on the 8th violates the 'by the 5th' deadline rule; it does not prove data inaccuracy or affect other clinics.

q: Read the policy statement: 'Civil service competency assessment aims not merely to audit past credentials, but to verify practical readiness to deliver equitable, citizen-centered outcomes.' What is the primary purpose emphasized?
options: Evaluating real-world capability to serve citizens fairly and effectively.
Replacing all university degrees and professional licenses.
Reducing the total number of public health facilities.
Focusing exclusively on theoretical textbook definitions.
rationale: The phrase 'practical readiness to deliver equitable, citizen-centered outcomes' highlights applied job capability over mere credential counting.

q: Applying the 5S Kaizen principle (Sort, Set in Order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain) in an emergency triage room, what is the very first step your team should take?
options: Sort (Seiri): Separate essential, frequently used emergency supplies from expired, broken, or unnecessary items cluttering the workspace.
Standardize (Seiketsu): Print new wall posters before cleaning the cabinets.
Set in Order (Seiton): Buy extra storage shelves before checking what is currently in the room.
Sustain (Shitsuke): Conduct an annual audit before organizing the shelves.
rationale: In 5S Kaizen, 'Sort' always comes first—removing unneeded and expired items creates space before organizing and standardizing.

q: A public hospital displays a Citizen Charter at its main entrance specifying maximum waiting times for triage (15 minutes) and outpatient consultation (45 minutes). What is the primary governance purpose of this charter?
options: To establish transparent service standards and empower citizens to hold the facility accountable.
To advertise private consultation fees to incoming patients.
To discourage patients with minor illnesses from visiting the hospital.
To exempt staff from documenting patient arrival times.
rationale: Citizen Charters set clear, measurable service commitments so both staff and the public know expected standards and grievance channels.

q: During a review of woreda health indicators, you notice institutional delivery rates are 88%, while postnatal care (PNC) within 48 hours drops to 41%. What is the most strategic intervention?
options: Integrate structured 48-hour PNC scheduling into discharge workflows and link mothers directly with local Health Extension Workers for home follow-up.
Focus only on increasing institutional delivery rates above 95%.
Stop tracking PNC indicators until delivery rates reach 100%.
Ask mothers to return to the hospital six months after delivery.
rationale: Strategic thinking uses data gaps to strengthen continuum-of-care linkages between facility discharge and community follow-up.

q: Two suppliers bid to provide standard examination gloves to a public health bureau. Supplier A offers certified quality meeting Ethiopian FDA standards at 420 ETB/box; Supplier B offers unverified gloves at 350 ETB/box with high tearing rates. Which choice reflects true 'Value for Money'?
options: Selecting Supplier A, because Value for Money balances quality, safety, and durability rather than choosing the lowest upfront price.
Selecting Supplier B solely because 350 ETB is the lowest bid.
Splitting the order equally without checking quality certifications.
Canceling procurement until glove prices drop below 300 ETB.
rationale: In public procurement, Value for Money optimizes economy, efficiency, and effectiveness—cheap, defective medical supplies increase waste and infection risk.

q: During a multidisciplinary case review, a junior nurse notices a potential medication dosage discrepancy in a treatment plan written by a senior clinician. What is the safest, most constructive team action?
options: Speak up respectfully and promptly before administration, referencing the patient's weight/protocol to verify the dose together.
Administer the written dose without question to respect seniority.
Refuse to give the medication and leave the ward without informing anyone.
Wait until the next day's shift handover to mention the discrepancy.
rationale: Psychological safety and patient-centered teamwork require speaking up respectfully across hierarchies to prevent clinical errors.

q: Under Ethiopian civil service performance management rules, how should individual staff appraisals be conducted?
options: Objectively against pre-agreed measurable targets, behavioral competencies, and documented evidence throughout the appraisal period.
Based solely on personal friendship or seniority without reviewing work outputs.
Only when an employee applies for a transfer to another ministry.
Without sharing the evaluation criteria or feedback with the employee.
options.rationale: Merit-based civil service reform ties evaluations to transparent, pre-agreed KPIs and behavioral standards with constructive feedback.
